message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | Key Points | |------|------------------------|------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Must be returned within 30 days after you move out (unless you give a written notice of intent to stay).
• Landlord may keep up to one month’s rent for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Landlord must provide an itemized list of deductions.
• If you dispute, you can file a claim in small‑claims court. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Repairs for plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural issues must be made promptly. | • Texas Property Code §92.001 requires landlords to keep premises in good repair. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease must specify rent amount, due date, security deposit, lease duration, and any rules.
• Oral leases are enforceable but harder to prove. | • Texas law allows “month‑to‑month” tenancy if no fixed term is specified. | | **Rent Increases** | • For month‑to‑month tenants, landlord must give at least 30 days’ written notice before raising rent.
• For fixed‑term leases, rent can’t be increased until the lease expires unless both parties agree. | • Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or by mail. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a written notice: 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violation, 60 days for no‑cause termination of month‑to‑month.
• After notice, landlord files a lawsuit; you have 5 days to respond. | • Eviction can only proceed after a court judgment. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Landlord cannot enter without proper notice (usually 24 hours) except in emergencies. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • These protections are enforced under the Texas Fair Housing Act and federal Fair Housing Act. | | **Repair and Deduct / Rent Withhold** | • If landlord fails to make necessary repairs, you may:
1. Pay the repair yourself and deduct the cost from rent (up to $500).
2. Withhold rent until repairs are made (but you must give notice and follow procedure). | • Use the “repair and deduct” method only if the repair cost is less than $500 and you notify the landlord in writing. | | **Access to Records** | • You can request copies of your lease, security deposit receipts, and any notices. | • Landlord must provide them within a reasonable time. | | **Tenant Insurance** | • While not required by Texas law, it’s highly recommended to protect personal property. | • Some landlords may require proof of insurance for certain types of rentals. | --- #### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Get Everything in Writing** - Keep copies of the lease, any amendments, security deposit receipts, and communication with the landlord. 2. **Document Problems** - Take photos or videos of maintenance issues. - Keep a log of dates and times when you reported problems. 3. **Know the Notice Requirements** - For rent increases or lease termination, the landlord must give written notice at least 30 days in advance. - For nonpayment, a 3‑day notice is required. 4. **Respond Promptly to Notices** - If you receive a notice of eviction or lease violation, reply in writing and keep a copy. 5. **Seek Legal Assistance Early** - If you believe your landlord is violating your rights, contact a local tenant‑rights organization or a lawyer. - Texas has several nonprofit groups that offer free or low‑cost legal help. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Information on landlord‑tenant disputes, how to file complaints. | | **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** | Guidance on fair housing, tenant rights. | | **Local Legal Aid Societies** | Free legal advice and representation for low‑income tenants. | | **Texas Small Claims Court** | Process for filing claims up to $20,000 (including security deposit disputes). | | **National Apartment Association (NAA) – Texas Chapter** | Educational materials, tenant‑rights guides. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In - [ ] Read the lease thoroughly. - [ ] Verify the security deposit amount and conditions for its return. - [ ] Confirm the landlord’s contact information and emergency procedures. - [ ] Check for any existing damage and document it. - [ ] Ask about the landlord’s policy on repairs and maintenance. --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, timely notice for rent changes or lease termination, protection against discrimination, and the ability to seek remedies if your landlord fails to meet obligations. Keeping records, understanding notice periods, and knowing where to seek help are key to safeguarding those rights.
